chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the two of them, and he said: “They are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition), so if you forget them, there is no repetition upon you.”

key_terms.إِعَادَةٌ: repetition of the act, meaning performing it again
key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the recommended prophetic practice, as distinct from what is obligatory
key_terms.سَأَلْتُهُ: I asked him, introducing the Imam's answer
key_terms.نَسِيتَهُمَا: you forgot the two matters being referred to

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets a sunnah act in wudu (ablution), must the wudu be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the two matters being asked about are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition), not from the obligatory elements. Therefore, if a person forgets them, he is not required to repeat the act of worship. The narration is relevant to the rulings of wudu (ablution) and distinguishes recommended acts from obligatory ones.
